about: Roppongi's well-known landmarks that the game models by hand (src/game/landmarks/). Each one is also a place in people's day plans: scripts/life/places.mjs adds it to public/life/<area>/places.json (or, when OpenStreetMap already gave the same spot a place, tags that place and keeps its id so older plans still work). `life` is the kind of place it is for people's days (sight, office, shop, cafe, park, ...). `meet`: a classic meeting point, so groups can arrange to meet there. Position from `osm` (node/way id in data/<area>.osm.json, with `osmType`) or `lat`/`lon`. `door` (lat/lon) is where people stand when they go there, if not the place's own point. Photos were used as reference only; none are in this repo.

landmarks.note: The pink café on the corner of Roppongi Crossing, the neighborhood's classic meeting point (アマンド前で待ち合わせ).
Louise Bourgeois's 9.3 m bronze spider on 66 Plaza at the foot of Mori Tower, with 32 marble eggs. Placed in 2003 as a meeting spot like Hachiko: クモの下で会いましょう.

landmarks.ja: 六本木ヒルズ森タワー
landmarks.note: 54-floor, 238 m office tower at the heart of Roppongi Hills (2003). Tokyo City View and the Mori Art Museum are in the glass crown at the top.

landmarks.ja: ドン・キホーテ六本木店
landmarks.note: The 8-storey Don Quijote (ドンキ) on Gaien-Higashi-dori, open 24 hours, with fish tanks by the entrance and the half-pipe roller coaster on the roof that never ran (built 2005-06, neighbours objected to the noise). You can walk into the ground floor.

Kisho Kurokawa's museum (2007) behind the great undulating glass wall. Inside the glass is a tall atrium with two inverted concrete cones: Brasserie Paul Bocuse Le Musée sits on top of the big one, the Salon de Thé Rond on the small one. No permanent collection; it hosts big touring shows. You can walk into the atrium.
